title: LibraryItem
description: One library item. Exactly one of the part fields is set: it names the item's kind.

camera.description: A camera design: optics (when physical), the as-built model and the image size.

id.description: The item's id: its file stem.

origin.description: Where this copy came from, when it was copied into a project (version 2).

CameraChoice.description: The camera model of a stage and what of it stays fixed.

CameraParams.description: Serializable camera parameters for building a runtime model.

intrinsics.description: Pinhole intrinsics (`fx, fy, cx, cy` in pixels).

CameraTemplate.description: The camera model of every position of a layout.

optics.description: The cameras' physical optics, if they have them (ADR 0008).

oneOf.description:
OpenCV's modern layout: markers on the white squares, numbered row by
row.

FixLists.description:
The parameters held fixed in the solve, by calibration-rs's names per slot. A slot left out
keeps calibration-rs's default for the model.

oneOf.description: The whole lens moves along its axis; its focal length does not change.

Freedoms.description:
What else a stage estimates or holds, beyond the camera. Each is calibration-rs's option of
the same meaning; one that does not apply to the stage's workflow is refused. Absent, the
workflow's default holds.

fix_handeye.description: Hold the hand-eye in the joint laser solve (`rig_handeye_laserline`).

fix_poses.description:
The target poses (view indices) held at their linear estimate (`planar_intrinsics`,
`laserline_device`).

fix_target.description: Hold the target's pose in the joint laser solve (`rig_handeye_laserline`).

min_motion_angle_deg.description: The least robot rotation between views the linear hand-eye uses, degrees.

refine_intrinsics.description: Refine the intrinsics jointly with the rig and the hand-eye (rig workflows).

refine_rig.description: Refine the cameras' poses in the rig during the hand-eye solve (`rig_handeye`).

refine_robot_poses.description: Refine each view's robot pose under a prior (hand-eye workflows).

refine_sensor.description: Refine a Scheimpflug sensor's tilt jointly with the rig (rig workflows).

robot_rot_sigma_rad.description: The robot-pose prior's rotation σ, radians.

robot_trans_sigma_m.description: The robot-pose prior's translation σ, metres.

FxFyCxCy.description:
Standard pinhole intrinsics: focal lengths and principal point in pixels.

The pixel grid is assumed orthogonal, so `K` carries no skew term.

cx.description: Principal point X coordinate in pixels.

cy.description: Principal point Y coordinate in pixels.

fx.description: Focal length in pixels along X.

fy.description: Focal length in pixels along Y.

HeadDesign.description: A laser-triangulation head: a camera design and a line laser fixed to the camera's body.

camera.description: The camera: physical (its `optics` set), as a head's analyses need.

camera_se3_laser.description:
The laser's pose in the camera's body frame (its fan in the laser's `y–z` plane,
opening about `+z`).

fan_length_m.description:
Fan radius, metres: how far the fan reaches from the laser, the same
along every ray.

HeadWindow.description: Where a head must work: a window in its laser plane, measured from the laser's origin.

max_blur_px.description: The largest acceptable blur (geometric and diffraction), pixels.

near_m.description: Nearest range along the laser's central ray, metres.

width_m.description: Width along the laser line, centred on the central ray, metres.

ImageX.description: The direction of a ring camera's image +X.

oneOf.description:
The rig's +X, as each camera sees it: classical stereo. For two cameras on the rig's x
axis the image rows line up (the image +Y axes are the same); with no tilt (a parallel
rig) the image +X axes are the same too.

Iso3Schema.description:
JSON Schema proxy for [`Iso3`] (`nalgebra::Isometry3<f64>`).

`nalgebra` does not implement [`schemars::JsonSchema`], so `*Export` and
parameter types that embed [`Iso3`] annotate the field with
`#[cfg_attr(feature = "schemars", schemars(with = "Iso3Schema"))]`
(or `Vec<Iso3Schema>` / `Option<Iso3Schema>`). This proxy mirrors the exact
serde wire format of `Isometry3`:
`{ "rotation": [qx, qy, qz, qw], "translation": [tx, ty, tz] }`.

It exists only to describe that shape to `schemars`; it is never
constructed at runtime.

rotation.description: Unit quaternion `[qx, qy, qz, qw]` (i, j, k, w order).

ItemOrigin.description: Where a project's copy of an item came from (ADR 0010 §3).

layer.description: The layer it was copied from.

sha256.description: The source's content hash (`etendue_core::library::content_hash`) when it was copied.

ItemSource.description: Where an item's data comes from: its datasheet, for people.

notes.description: Anything else: how a value was measured, what was assumed.

azimuth_rad.description: Azimuth of laser `i` relative to camera `i`, radians (unused with `camera_se3_laser`).

camera_se3_laser.description:
Each laser fixed to its camera's body at this pose, as a head carries it; otherwise it
stands on the ring, aimed at the working point.

fan_length.description:
Fan radius, metres: how far the fan reaches from the laser, the same
along every ray.

radius_m.description: Distance of each laser from the rig axis, metres (unused with `camera_se3_laser`).

waist_distance_m.description:
Distance from the laser origin to the waist along each ray, metres:
where a focusable laser is focused. Absent, the waist is at the laser.

beam_waist_m.description: Beam-waist `1/e²` radius across the line, metres, when known.

Layer.description: A library layer (ADR 0010 §1) an item can be copied from.

LensOptics.description: An ideal thick lens with its entrance pupil.

entrance_pupil_m.description: Signed distance from H to the entrance pupil, metres (positive toward the object).

f_number.description: f-number: the focal length over the entrance pupil diameter.

name.description: What the lens is, e.g. `Kowa LM25HC`.

principal_gap_m.description:
Signed distance from the rear principal point H′ to the front one H, metres (positive
when H lies on the object side).

LensPart.description: A lens: what a datasheet gives, and the thick-lens data the camera model needs.

entrance_pupil_m.description: Signed distance from H to the entrance pupil, metres (`0` when unknown).

fov_diagonal_deg.description: Diagonal field of view on the sensor it was specified for, degrees.

min_f_number.description: The widest aperture: the smallest f-number.

mtf50_lp_mm.description: Spatial frequency at 50 % MTF, line pairs per millimetre.

principal_gap_m.description: Signed distance from H′ to H, metres (`0` when unknown: a thin lens).

Loss.description: A robust loss, as calibration-rs names it.

oneOf.description: Huber, with its scale (pixels for reprojection).

MarkerCircle.description: A marker board circle: on square `(i, j)` (column, row), white or black.

MountPart.description:
A rigid adapter on a robot's tool flange (ADR 0010 §5): what a rig or a target is mounted
through, eye-in-hand or eye-to-hand.

flange_se3_device.description: The mounted device's frame in the flange's frame.

mass_kg.description: Mass, kilograms, for the payload budget.

focus_distance_m.description:
Distance from the image-plane datum to the plane in focus, metres, as a lens's focus scale
reads it.

tilt_rad.description:
The sensor's tilt `[τx, τy]` about the image-plane datum, radians, in calibration-rs's
(OpenCV's) convention.

oneOf.description: A white disk on a dark square.
A black disk on a light square.

PrintedTarget.description:
A target as calib-targets prints it, tagged on `kind`. Sizes are in
millimetres, as on the print.

Planar targets lie in the target frame's `z = 0` plane, centred on its
origin, facing +Z, the print's top edge at +Y. A PuzzlePole is a cylinder:
its frame is calib-targets' pole object frame (axis +Z, origin on the axis
in the plane of axial corner 0, the seam at +X).

inner_square_rel.description: White inset in the black squares, as a fraction of the side.
White inset in the plain black squares, as a fraction of the side.

marker_size_rel.description: Marker side as a fraction of the square side.

oneOf.description: A chessboard with three circles that fix its origin and orientation.

circle_diameter_rel.description: Circle diameter as a fraction of the square side.

inner_square_rel.description: White inset in the black squares, as a fraction of the side.

oneOf.description:
A PuzzleBoard: a chessboard whose edge dots make every corner
self-identifying.

dot_diameter_rel.description: Edge-dot diameter as a fraction of the square side.

origin_col.description: Master column of the board's first square.

origin_row.description: Master row of the board's first square.

oneOf.description:
A PuzzlePole: a PuzzleBoard strip wrapped around a cylinder of
circumference `circumference_squares × square_size_mm`.

axial_start_col.description: Master column the strip is cut from.

circumference_squares.description:
Squares around the circumference: a supported period (12, 18,
24, 30, 36 or 42).

dot_diameter_rel.description: Edge-dot diameter as a fraction of the square side.

start_row.description:
Master row the strip is cut from (the seam); must match the
period (see calib-targets `PuzzlePolePeriod`).

ProcedurePart.description: A calibration procedure: stages in order. The last stage's result is the procedure's.

image_x.description: Which way each camera's image +X points.

lasers.description: One laser per camera, if any.

phase_rad.description: Azimuth of camera 0 about the rig axis, radians.

radius_m.description:
Distance of each camera from the rig axis, metres (`0` only for one
camera).

tilt_rad.description:
Angle between each camera's axis and the rig axis, radians; default
`atan(radius / working_distance)`.

working_distance_m.description:
Where the camera axes meet the rig axis (with the default tilt), and
where the lasers aim: `(0, 0, working_distance_m)` in the rig frame.

Seed.description: Where a stage's starting value of an estimate comes from.

oneOf.description:
The design, as a user would enter it from datasheets: the focal length rounded to 100 px,
the principal point at the image centre, no distortion, the tilt about x rounded to a
whole degree.
The truth (synthetic datasets only; the report says so).
An earlier stage's estimate, by the stage's id.

Seeds.description: What a stage starts from. Absent, the workflow's own linear initialisation.

intrinsics.description: Focal lengths and principal points (and with them the distortion).

planes.description:
The laser planes, one per camera in its frame (laser workflows): the design's (nominal or
truth: in a simulation the design is the truth) or an earlier stage's estimate.

rig.description:
The cameras' poses in the rig: from an earlier rig stage only (calibration-rs takes the
target's pose per view with them). A `rig_handeye_laserline` stage takes a `rig_handeye`
stage's whole result here (its cameras, rig and hand-eye) as the joint solve's start.

SensorChoice.description: The sensor model a stage calibrates.

oneOf.description: What the design has: Scheimpflug when a camera's sensor tilts, identity otherwise.

name.description: What the sensor is, e.g. `Sony IMX174`.

oneOf.description: Homography applied in the sensor plane.

h.description: Row-major homography matrix mapping normalized to sensor coordinates.

tilt_x.description: Tilt around X axis in radians (alias: tau_x).

tilt_y.description: Tilt around Y axis in radians (alias: tau_y).

SolverChoice.description: How a stage solves. Absent fields keep the workflow's defaults.

max_iters.description: Iteration limit of the non-linear solve.

robust_loss.description: The robust loss on the reprojection residuals.

camera.description:
The camera a single-camera stage calibrates, by scene id; absent, the dataset's only
camera (a stage per camera repeats with each id). Rig stages take every camera.

id.description: Its id, unique in the procedure; later stages seed from it by this id.

model.description: The camera model and its fixed parameters.

oneOf.description:
A calibration board, described in the calibration-rs dataset
vocabulary (the same `TargetSpec` a synthetic `DatasetSpec` emits).
The board is centred on the local origin in the `z = 0` plane, facing
+Z. The in-plane mapping from board (feature) coordinates to the
target frame is defined once, by `etendue-synth`: the printed board
reads correctly from +Z, its top edge at +Y.

board.description:
Board layout (`kind`-tagged: chessboard, charuco, puzzleboard,
ringgrid).

oneOf.description:
A target as calib-targets prints it — chessboard, ChArUco, marker
board, PuzzleBoard, or the PuzzlePole cylinder — with its print
parameters (millimetres). Unlike `board`, every kind is drawn,
ground-truthed and detected; only those calibration-rs takes go into
a calibration dataset.

A plain rectangle centred on the local origin in the `z = 0` plane
(the `etendue-core` `TargetEntity`).

height.description: Extent along local Y, in metres.

width.description: Extent along local X, in metres.

geometry.description: What it is, as a scene target holds it.

oneOf.description:
Standard checkerboard. Counts are interior corners
(i.e. `9x6` ⇒ a 10×7 black-and-white square grid).

A plain chessboard has no markers: each view is labelled from the
detection's own top-left corner. Where views share one target frame
(single-camera hand-eye and every rig topology) the runner therefore
keeps a view only when its corners reach every edge of the board.
In a rig, each camera's labels are turned to agree with the other
cameras of the view, so a board seen turned is kept. Where the target
is fixed through the views (hand-eye), the board must appear the same
way up in every image of camera 0 (`cols` across and `rows` down);
a board seen turned by 90° is dropped, and one seen upside down, or a
square board seen turned by 90°, cannot be told apart. Use a ChArUco
or PuzzleBoard target to calibrate a shared frame from partial views.

cols.description:
Number of interior corners across the board (the image's
columns axis when the board is seen as declared).

rows.description:
Number of interior corners down the board (the image's rows
axis when the board is seen as declared).

square_size_m.description: Edge length of one square in metres.

oneOf.description:
ChArUco board. Marker IDs and dictionary live here so detection
is fully deterministic from the manifest.

cols.description: Number of squares along the cols axis.

dictionary.description:
ArUco dictionary identifier (e.g. `"DICT_4X4_50"`). The
detector validates this against the supported set.

marker_size_m.description: Edge length of an embedded marker in metres.

rows.description:
Number of squares along the rows axis (full grid, not
interior corners).

square_size_m.description: Edge length of one square in metres.

oneOf.description:
Puzzleboard target: a self-identifying chessboard. The layout name
carries the board's dimensions, so the manifest fully determines
detection.

cell_size_m.description: Edge length of one cell in metres.

layout.description:
Board dimensions as `puzzle_<rows>x<cols>` (e.g.
`"puzzle_12x12"`; the `puzzle_` prefix is optional).

oneOf.description:
Coded ring-grid target (the `ringgrid` crate). The board is a
hex-lattice of self-identifying ring markers; its geometry mirrors
`ringgrid::BoardLayout` so the manifest fully determines detection.

long_row_cols.description:
Number of columns in the longest (even-indexed) row. Shorter
rows are derived by the hex-lattice layout.

marker_ring_width_m.description: Width of each ring band in metres.

pitch_m.description: Center-to-center spacing between adjacent markers in metres.
